newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pressures on HK trade growth seen easing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pressures on HK trade growth seen easing in 1997.

text.p: Many of the factors that weighed on Hong Kong's trade performance last year have eased, a senior trade official said on Monday.
"The economy revived late last year and improved a lot from the beginning of the year," Alan Lai, director general of trade, told a news conference.
Some factors that hit the territory's trade last year, including Sino-Taiwanese tension and Sino-U.S. disputes over intellectual property rights, were no longer pressing, he added.
Lai declined to make forecasts for the territory's trade performance in 1997.
Total trade in goods in 1996 is forecast at HK$2,958 billion in value, representing an increase of about five percent in real terms, Lai said.

Re-exports are expected to have increased about eight percent in real terms to HK$1,196 billion last year. Domestic exports are forecast to have fallen a real 7.5 percent to HK$214 billion in 1996, after a two percent rise in 1995.
Total exports are expected to have grown about a real 5.4 percent to HK$1,410 billion in 1996, lower than the 12 percent growth in 1995.
Exports of services are expected to have risen about 12 percent in value to HK$325 billion in 1996 while imports of services are forecast to have grown about five percent in value.
Total trade in services is expected to have increased a real five percent to about HK$497 billion in 1996, versus nine percent in 1995.
Total trade in goods and services is expected to be up about five percent in real terms to HK$3,455 billion in 1996.

Factors that weakened export performance for 1996 included the relative strength of the Hong Kong dollar, a slow-down in import demand in the U.S. and China, Sino-Taiwanese tension early in the year, and Sino-U.S. dispute over intellectual property rights protection, Lai said.
Trade diversion effect of the North American Free Trade Agreement and the abrupt downturn in the electronic product cycle had also affected Hong Kong trade in 1996, he added.
